Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:29: The Fourth [Reason] – when the correction of his soul is delayed, iniquity will befall him and he will continually stumble in transgressions.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:30: The Fifth [Reason] – through delaying the correction of the soul, the inclination grows ever stronger, and it becomes harder for him to correct his soul afterward, as it is written (Proverbs 24:31), "and behold, it was all overgrown with thistles, etc." And our Sages of blessed memory said: once the inclination becomes bound up with a transgression, it becomes like a matter of heresy, and he will no longer have the power to purify himself of it. And they said in the ethical teachings: habit rules over everything.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:31: The Sixth [Reason] – perhaps his days will not continue, and he will die before he completes the obligation of teshuvah; therefore Solomon the king, peace upon him, warned (Ecclesiastes 9:8), "At all times let your garments be white."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:32: The Seventh [Reason] – by delaying his teshuvah, his iniquities become old to him and he forgets their grief, and he no longer worries over them as he did at first.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:33: The Eighth [Reason] – when he advances in years and the strength of his inclination is weakened, he will not receive reward for teshuvah as he would have for correcting his heart in the days of his youth. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Avodah Zarah 19a): "Fortunate is the man who fears the Lord" — while he is still a man [in his vigor]. And they said: when the hand of the thief can no longer steal, he regards his own soul as an honest man's.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 2:34: The Ninth [Reason] – in the days of old age, when the power of his senses is lacking, he no longer has the strength to lay new paths in his heart, and to marshal thoughts to do battle with his inclination in order to attain the virtues, to labor and toil in Torah and in good deeds — as it is written (Ecclesiastes 12:1), "Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near of which you will say, I have no delight in them." Therefore it is fitting for a man to hasten a way of escape for his soul, as it is said (Psalms 119:60), "I hastened, and delayed not, to keep Your commandments."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:1:
Gate Three – On the Explanation of the Severity of the Commandments, the Prohibitions, and the Distinctions Among the Punishments.
Since the penitent has been warned to search his ways, and to know how many are his iniquities and sins, and after the search has been completed, he has been further warned to investigate the gravity of each and every one of his sins, as it is said (Lamentations 3:40), "Let us search and examine our ways" — so that he come to know the full extent of every sin he has committed, and how greatly he has multiplied guilt through it; for there is guilt that reaches unto the heavens in its greatness, and there is evil that is weighed as equal to many great sins. And the teshuvah is great in proportion to the greatness of such searchings of the heart, for according to his knowledge of the abundance and greatness of the iniquity, his soul will grieve over it; only then will their uncircumcised heart submit, and only then will they find their iniquity accepted.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:2: Furthermore, the investigation of the intensity of the iniquity is of avail in covering his humiliated face when he asks for forgiveness, as it is said (Ezra 9:6), "O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to You, my God"; and in wrapping himself in shame before the Blessed Name, even after he trusts in His forgiveness, as it is said (Ezekiel 16:63), "that you may remember and be ashamed... when I have forgiven you for all that you have done"; and in keeping ever before his eyes the greatness of the kindness of atonement, as it is said (Psalms 26:3), "for Your kindness is before my eyes." And the parable for this: if a servant sinned against his master and comes to submit before him, his master's soul is not drawn toward the servant except after he comes to know the weight of his own transgression; and if he pictures to himself that the sin is a trivial matter, the wrath against him will grow greater. Therefore the sinner is obligated to recognize the intensity of the sin and its punishment, as it is said (I Samuel 26:21), "Behold, I have played the fool and have erred exceedingly." Therefore we have needed to teach the children of Judah, for instruction and for testimony, the severity of the punishments for every iniquity and every sin; hence all the words of this introduction. And there is a further sublime and firmly-established benefit: for I have indeed seen that most of the people think of many grave transgressions as though they were light, and regard the transgressions liable to death or excision as though carefulness about them were merely an extra measure of piety or a mark of special saintliness — and they stumble in them unwittingly, with no one to rebuke them, as it is said (Isaiah 48:8), "even from of old your ear was not opened." Therefore we have needed to warn them and to open their ears concerning the severity of many transgressions, and that even in the light commandments there are many paths and aspects leading to utter destruction and the loss of the soul. And many of the wicked will abandon their way once they know the loss and the damage it entails, once the greatness of the sin and what has been decreed for it is revealed to them; and those who have stumbled will gird themselves with strength to conquer their desire, for how could they continue, once they see the loss of their own soul?
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:3: And the parable for this is a man who wishes to go to a certain city, and they tell him that the road is beset with thorns, snares, and stumbling-stones, yet because he needs to reach that place, he does not cease from going; but should they tell him that a lion is on the road and a leopard lies in wait for him, then he will keep his feet from that road entirely. Therefore Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 1:2), "To know wisdom and instruction (musar), to understand." Its meaning: proper conduct in deed and the abandonment of transgressions are called "wisdom," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:6), "for it is your wisdom and your understanding." And after one has learned and knows the commandments and what the transgressions are, he must also learn the disgrace of the transgressions, and the loss and destruction found in them, so as to distance his soul from them, and to rebuke himself by remembering the punishments, and to discipline others as well; and this knowledge is called "musar," and it will be pleasant for those who rebuke to learn and know this.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:4: Now let us explain the levels of the severity of the commandments, the prohibitions, and the distinctions among the punishments. The First Level – the Severity of the Words of the Sages (Divrei Sofrim): We have been obligated by the Torah to accept the enactments of the prophets and the judges, and to hear the words of the Sages and to be careful within their fences, as it is said (Deuteronomy 17:11), "You shall not turn aside from the word which they tell you, to the right hand or to the left." And even though we have been warned by the Torah to accept upon ourselves to do all that they instruct us, nevertheless the positive commandment of the Torah is graver than their words, since the essential matter is stated explicitly in the Book of God's Torah and the Blessed Name has commanded it specifically. Yet there are ways and aspects in which the words of the Sages will be found more severe than the words of the Torah, as our Sages of blessed memory said: the words of the Sages are more severe than the words of the Torah — for one who says there is no obligation of tefillin, so as to transgress the words of the Torah, is exempt [from lashes]; but one who says there should be five compartments, adding to the words of the Sages, is liable. And whoever transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:5: Now, you ought to know why one who transgresses the words of the Sages is more liable than one who transgresses a positive or negative commandment [of the Torah]. And this is the explanation of the matter: one who transgresses the words of the Sages, whose heart is full enough to act so, does so because their commandment seems light in his eyes — not because his inclination has overpowered him, but because his eyes have grown too dim to see the light of their words, and he does not walk by the brightness of the faith, nor has he taken upon himself the yoke of its decree, nor does he trouble himself to fulfill their statement, since it is not written in the Book of the Torah; and he does not behave as does one who transgresses the words of the Torah, whose soul is bitter to him and who feels disgust with himself, and fears and is distressed that his inclination led him astray to sin. Therefore a sentence of death shall be upon such a man, for he has cast off one item from among all the good things given to him, and it is as though he said, Let us break their bonds asunder; and this is comparable to what is written concerning the elder who defies the ruling of the Sages (Deuteronomy 17:12), "And the man who acts presumptuously, not listening to the priest..."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:6: And the second reason: that man is far from teshuvah, since the matter is not grave in his eyes, for he continually repeats his folly; and the light sin, when the sinner stumbles in it many times over, incurs a punishment greater than the grave one.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:7: Our Sages of blessed memory further said: "Your love is better than wine" — the words of the Sages are more beloved than the wine of the Torah. And we must explain this too. Know well that the fear of the Lord is the foundation of the commandments, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:12), "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear the Lord your God"; and through this the Lord is pleased with His creatures, as it is said (Psalms 147:10-11), "The Lord is pleased with those who fear Him." And the enactments of the Sages and their fences are a foundation for the path of fear, for one erects a fence and a safeguard lest a person's hand come to touch what the Torah forbids — like the owner of a field who builds a fence around what is precious to him, out of fear that people might enter it and it would become a place for oxen to be driven through and sheep to trample, as it is said (Leviticus 18:30), "And you shall keep My charge" — meaning, make a safeguard for My charge. And the abundance of care, of fences, and of distancing oneself from what is forbidden — is this not among the very foundations of awe? And whoever multiplies his care will attain a great reward, as it is said (Psalms 19:12), "Moreover, by them is Your servant warned; in keeping them there is great reward." Therefore they said, "the words of the Sages are more beloved than the wine of the Torah" — for their fences and decrees are among the foundations of the fear of the Lord, and the commandment of fear carries reward equal to many commandments, since it is the foundation for them all. And the illustration of this matter: one who is careful to avoid seclusion with a woman, out of his own fear lest he stumble into iniquity, in accordance with what our Sages of blessed memory decreed — is this not because the light of the fear of the exalted God has shone upon his soul?
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:8: Now, we have already stated for you, in the Gate of Fear, that a person is obligated to look at his children and understand them, and to distinguish between the crooked and perverse and the one who walks uprightly, for the sublime benefit that we have made known to you. And behold, when you see men who are gluttonous, treating the washing of hands with contempt, sitting down to eat bread without reciting a blessing before eating and after eating, and the like — many words and enactments of the Sages whose fences they breach — by this they shall be tested; by this you shall know and examine their way, that they are exceedingly evil and sinful before the Lord, and that their end is unto destruction. And of them it was said that one who transgresses the words of the Sages is liable, for these deeds are not forced upon them by their inclination, nor does the nature of their material substance and physical desire compel them to sin in these matters — it is nothing but an evil heart and a casting off of the yoke of Heaven from their necks. And behold, they are like the whole multitude of the faction of the presumptuous, who say to God, "Depart from us, for we have no desire to know Your ways" — they too are far from the way of truth. So too the faction who are not careful about the cheese of gentiles and the cooking of gentiles, because the words of the Sages seem light in their eyes — even though they sin merely to fill their bellies, they have thereby despised the words of the Sages and broken the yoke of Torah and awe; of them too it was said that whoever transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death, as we have explained. And the second reason: since they know that the holy people are careful about all these things, they have deliberately set themselves apart from our people and separated themselves from the ways of the community. And our Sages of blessed memory said that those who separate themselves from the ways of the community descend to Gehinnom and are judged there for generations upon generations. And know that whoever transgresses the words of the Sages, his punishment is at the hand of the court, to be struck with lashes of rebellion (makkat mardut), according to what the eyes of the court saw fit to discipline and punish at that time, whether fewer than forty [lashes] or additional strikes beyond these.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:9: The Second Level – the Severity of Positive Commandments: the foundation of reward and the root of recompense in exchange for service lies in the fulfillment of positive commandments, as it is said (Proverbs 13:13), "but whoever fears a commandment will be rewarded," and it is said (Malachi 3:18), "Then you shall again discern between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who serves Him not." And the service is found in the commandments that depend on an action, whether they consist of nothing but a positive commandment, or whether they also carry with them a negative commandment, such as it is said (Deuteronomy 15:7), "You shall not harden your heart, etc." And the commandment of service will be explained, God willing, in the Gate of Service. However, there is also a way in which the reward for one who is careful not to transgress a negative commandment can attain the reward of one who performs a positive commandment — such as when a matter of transgression comes within a man's reach, and desire for an act of immorality arises, and he subdues his inclination, for this is among the foundations of the fear of the Blessed Name. And likewise one who has the opportunity to grow rich through fraud and deceit, with no one seeing and no one knowing, yet walks in his innocence and with clean hands — his reward for this is like one who sows for charity and toils in the performance of a mitzvah. And so it is written (Psalms 119:3), "They also do no iniquity; they walk in His ways." And our Sages of blessed memory said: since they did no iniquity, they walked in His ways — and we have already stated for you the explanation of this verse. And so our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever sat and did not commit a transgression is given reward as one who performed a mitzvah, as when a matter of transgression came within his reach and he was saved from it. They further said (Malachi 3:16), "for those who fear the Lord and who think upon His name" — this refers to one to whom a matter of transgression comes within reach, and he is saved from it. This reward, too, has as its essential foundation the positive commandment of subduing one's inclination through the fear of God, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "You shall fear the Lord your God." And our Sages of blessed memory said: be as careful with a light commandment as with a grave one, for you do not know the reward given for the commandments. Now, in the Torah it is explained what shall be done to anyone who transgresses a negative commandment, and punishments, laws, and a set procedure are apportioned to them — the punishments being forty lashes, death or excision at the hand of Heaven, and the four death penalties administered by the court. But the reward for each and every positive commandment is not spelled out in the Torah, so that people not cease to fulfill the light commandments and occupy themselves only with the grave ones.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:10: And they gave a parable for this concerning a king who told his servants to plant every delightful tree in his orchard, and said he would give them reward, but did not make known to them the reward for the planting of each and every tree — because the king desired that nothing be lacking in his orchard, so that they would plant in it a great many species of pleasant plantings; whereas had his servants known the reward for planting each and every tree of the orchard, they would then have devoted all their effort to the saplings whose reward was greater than the rest, in order to increase their own reward. So it is with the matter of the commandments: since the Name was pleased to grant merit to Israel through the fulfillment of all the commandments, to give them eternal life as an inheritance, and for all the commandments together to be a graceful wreath upon their heads — for when they complete the measure of their labor, their wage from Him shall be complete. Do you not know that our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever occupies himself with Torah alone is like one who has no God — even though they also said Torah study outweighs them all? And the reward of the light commandment is great and wondrous beyond measure or count. Behold, you see in the commandment of sending away the mother bird, which involves no toil and no expenditure of money, it is said of it (Deuteronomy 22:7), "that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days." And our Sages of blessed memory said: Rabbi Yaakov says, there is no commandment in the Torah so light that the resurrection of the dead is not made dependent on it, for it is said concerning the sending away of the mother bird, "that it may be well with you... and that you may prolong your days" — "that it may be well with you," in the world that is entirely good; "and that you may prolong your days," in the world that is entirely long. Now, if concerning a light commandment worth but a small coin the Torah spoke thus, how much more so concerning the grave commandments.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:11: Now let us speak concerning the punishment for the neglect of a positive commandment. Our Sages of blessed memory said: if a man was warned to make a sukkah or take up the lulav, and he does not do so, they strike him until his soul departs. And they said that men who have never in their lives placed tefillin upon their heads are called "rebels of Israel in their body," and their punishment is more severe than one who transgresses, on a single occasion, a matter liable to excision. And they said: whoever has more iniquities than merits, and among them the iniquity of "the rebels of Israel in their body" — such as one who never placed tefillin, or transgressors of transgressions such as sexual immorality — descend to Gehinnom on the day of judgment and are judged there for twelve months; after twelve months, their bodies are consumed and their souls are burned, and their spirit is scattered beneath the soles of the feet of the righteous, as it is said (Malachi 3:21), "and you shall tread down the wicked, for they shall be ashes, etc." And they said: whoever treats a positive commandment lightly in his own eyes — such as one who demeans the intermediate days of a festival, which carries a positive commandment, as it is said (Exodus 23:15), "You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread" — even if he possesses Torah and good deeds, he has no share in the World to Come. And every positive commandment carries with it a general prohibitive warning, as it is said (Deuteronomy 13:1), "You shall not add to it, nor take away from it."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:12: And the fulfillment of a positive commandment is called "fear of Heaven," just as is carefulness regarding a negative commandment, as it is said (Leviticus 19:32), "You shall rise up before the gray-headed, and honor the face of the old man, and you shall fear your God: I am the Lord." And it is said (Psalms 34:12), "I will teach you the fear of the Lord," and afterward it is said, "Turn from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it." From this we learn that whoever does not occupy himself with doing good and seeking peace has nullified the fear of Heaven, and he is among the wicked, for he does not fear God, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 8:13), "But it shall not be well with the wicked, nor shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:13: And among the positive commandments there are grave ones that the mass of the people are not careful about, such as the mentioning of the Name of Heaven in vain, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "You shall fear the Lord your God" — and our Sages of blessed memory said, we have been warned by this not to mention the Name of Heaven in vain. And likewise acts of kindness (gemilut chasadim), which is a positive commandment, as it is said (Exodus 18:20), "and you shall make known to them the way in which they shall walk" — this refers to acts of kindness. And they said: greater is the performance of acts of kindness than charity, for charity is given only to the poor, while acts of kindness may be done both for the poor and for the rich. Therefore they said, the world stands on three things: on Torah, on service [of God], and on the performance of acts of kindness. Now, charity is done with one's money, while acts of kindness may be done either with one's body or with one's money, for a person is obligated to trouble himself in seeking the good of his people, and to labor diligently for the benefit of his fellow, whether he is poor or rich. And this is among the gravest and most essential things demanded of a person, as it is said (Micah 6:8), "He has told you, man, what is good, and what the Lord requires of you: only to do justice and to love kindness." And it is likewise a commandment to go beyond the strict letter of the law, as it is said (Exodus 18:20), "and the deed that they must do" — and our Sages of blessed memory said, this refers to going beyond the strict letter of the law. And there are many ways in this matter in which this commandment will be among the gravest, all according to the circumstances of the case, as our Sages of blessed memory said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they insisted on the strict law of the Torah and did not go beyond the strict letter of the law.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:14: And there are many people among the multitude who think that the essence of destruction and loss of the soul lies only in transgressions that involve an actual deed, and that there is no loss of soul for a man who is pure of sinning in deed, has not walked in the way of transgressions, but has merely ceased from performing commandments and good deeds. Therefore we are obligated to inform those whose spirit of understanding has gone astray, that our Sages of blessed memory said: the Holy One, blessed be He, overlooked idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed, but did not overlook the iniquity of the neglect of Torah study. And they said: just as the reward for Torah study is greater than for all the other commandments, so too the punishment for one who neglects it is greater than for all the transgressions. And they said (Numbers 15:31), "Because he has despised the word of the Lord, and has broken His commandment" — this is said of one who is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not do so. And we have already mentioned all this to you in the Gate of Torah.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:15: And we find, concerning the men of Sodom, that they were exceedingly evil before the Lord in a number of corrupt practices, such as robbery and violence and perversion of justice and sexual immorality; and yet, with all this, Scripture mentions that they were lost and destroyed for the iniquity of neglecting acts of charity, as it is said (Ezekiel 16:49), "Behold, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, fullness of bread... and she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy." And it is said of people who do not set their thoughts continually to reflect on the fear of the Lord (Isaiah 29:13-14), "and their fear of Me is a commandment of men, learned by rote — therefore, behold, I will again do a marvelous work among this people, a marvel and a wonder." And it is said (Jeremiah 12:2), "Why does the way of the wicked prosper... You are near in their mouth, but far from their innermost thoughts." And it is said (Psalms 73:27), "For behold, those who are far from You shall perish."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:16: And know that in proportion to the greatness of the commandment, the punishment of one who fails to perform it grows greater, even though he does no actual deed in nullifying it — as we find with the commandment of the Passover offering and the commandment of circumcision, which are positive commandments and yet carry the punishment of excision.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:17: And know that the highest virtues have been entrusted to positive commandments, such as the virtue of choice, as it is said (Deuteronomy 30:19), "and you shall choose life"; and the virtue of Torah study, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:7), "and you shall speak of them"; and the virtue of walking in the ways of the Lord, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:9), "and you shall walk in His ways"; and the virtue of contemplating the greatness of the Lord, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:39), "And you shall know this day, and consider it in your heart, that the Lord, He is God" — and David said (Psalms 14:2), "The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of man, to see if there were any who understood, who sought God"; and the virtue of remembering His kindnesses and reflecting upon them, as it is said (Deuteronomy 8:2), "And you shall remember all the way," and it is said (Deuteronomy 8:5), "And you shall know in your heart, that just as a man chastens his son, the Lord your God chastens you" — and David said (Psalms 107:43), "and let them consider the kindnesses of the Lord," and it is said (Psalms 26:3), "for Your kindness is before my eyes"; and the virtue of holiness, as it is said (Leviticus 11:44), "and sanctify yourselves, and be holy"; and the virtue of service, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "Him shall you serve"; and the virtue of fear, as it is said (ibid.), "you shall fear the Lord your God"; and the virtue of love, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the Lord your God"; and the virtue of cleaving, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "and to Him shall you cleave." Each of these has many levels, as will be explained, God willing. And it is for the sake of these virtues that man was created, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory." And what hope has the creature if he does not set the labor of his soul and the essence of his occupation upon the things for the sake of which he was created?
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:18: And behold, the punishment for the neglect of a commandment is made clear in the Torah, as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:26), "Cursed be he who does not uphold the words of this Torah, to do them." Its saying "to do them" shows that this is said concerning the neglect of the performance of the commandment.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:19: And know that the creature is obligated to be a faithful messenger and an intelligent servant in every task of his Master's service. And the skilled laborer will be swift in his own work and will also watch over the work of his fellow laborers, keeping his eyes on their ways to see whether they perform it faithfully, warning them and instructing them in the work they must do — for his wish and desire is that his master's work be done without deceit; therefore he supports the hands of those doing the work. And our Sages of blessed memory said in the Sifrei, concerning "Cursed be he who does not uphold": a man who has learned, reviewed, and taught others, and fulfilled the Torah, and who has it in his power to support the hands of those who occupy themselves with Torah and mitzvot, yet did not support them — behold, he is included among those cursed who do not uphold.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:20: And among the grave commandments is the prohibition against litigating before the courts of the gentiles, as it is said (Exodus 21:1), "Now these are the judgments which you shall set before them" — before them, and not before gentiles; yet the transgressors stumble in this. And we have already spoken earlier concerning this transgression.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:21: And concerning the neglect of reverence for father and mother, which is a positive commandment, as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:16), "Cursed be he who dishonors his father or his mother" — the matter of "dishonors" is one who treats their honor with contempt and nullifies their reverence, as our Sages of blessed memory said (Kiddushin 32a): "Every man shall revere his mother and his father" — what is reverence for a father? He does not sit in his place, does not contradict his words, and does not decide against him [in a dispute].
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:22: And the commandment of tefillin and the commandment of mezuzah are positive commandments, and they are included among the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, since they are written in the passage of the Shema. And from this you may understand the punishment of one who neglects these commandments, for he breaks the yoke and severs the bonds; and we have already spoken earlier of these commandments. And concerning the commandment of tzitzit, our Sages of blessed memory said in the Sifrei that the tzitzit add holiness, as it is said (Numbers 15:40), "that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God." And even though the commandment of tzitzit applies only to one who has a garment with four corners, and if he has no such garment he is not obligated to acquire one, nevertheless our Sages of blessed memory said that he will surely be punished in times of trouble for not having desired in his heart the beauty of the commandment and its reward, so as to avoid the circumstance of his obligation and acquire for himself a four-cornered garment to make tzitzit on its corners.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:23: And know that one who fears the word of the Lord will be strict and precise, and will place his very soul in his palm, over a light commandment just as over the grave ones — for they do not consider the fact that this commandment is light in comparison to the graver ones, but rather consider the greatness of Him, blessed be He, who warned concerning it. Open your eyes well to see that this honored foundation is set forth in the Torah, for it is written concerning the commandment of rising before the aged, just as it is written concerning the commandment of reverence for one's father and mother and the observance of the Sabbath: "I am the Lord." And we have brought to this place, established for each one in this book, many of the commandments which many of the people found in this generation fall short in performing. Take them, then, to yourself and onto the tablet of your heart.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:24: The Third Level – a Prohibition Convertible into a Positive Commandment: our Sages of blessed memory said, for a prohibition convertible into a positive commandment, one is not lashed — such as (Deuteronomy 22:6), "You shall not take the mother together with the young," which is converted into a positive commandment, as it is said (Deuteronomy 22:7), "You shall surely let go [the mother]." And even though one is not lashed at the hand of the court for these, some among them carry a punishment that is grave, reaching unto the heavens, whose judgment rises unto the skies — such as robbery, as it is said (Leviticus 19:13), "You shall not rob," which is converted into a positive commandment (Leviticus 5:23), "and he shall restore that which he robbed." And they said: the sentence of the generation of the Flood was sealed only because of robbery, as it is said (Genesis 6:13), "The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence." And even though sexual immorality is graver than robbery, the measure of punishment for robbery is to bring near the day of its doom and hasten its future. And they further said: for a measure filled with iniquities, no prosecutor accuses as does robbery. And Solomon the king, peace upon him, said concerning treasures of deceit and fraud (Proverbs 21:6), "The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor of those who seek death." Its meaning: treasures of deceit and fraud are a fleeting vapor, for their end is destruction; and even while still in his possession, they are hostile to him and seek the life of their owner and bring about his death — in the sense of what Habakkuk, peace upon him, said (Habakkuk 2:9), "Woe to him who gets evil gain for his house... for the stone shall cry out from the wall, etc." And the robbery of the poor incurs the death penalty at the hand of Heaven, as it is said (Proverbs 22:22-23), "Rob not the poor, because he is poor, neither oppress the afflicted in the gate: for the Lord will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those who spoil them." Its meaning: do not rob the poor man because he is poor and has no one to help him, and do not oppress the poor man in the gate through humiliation and disgrace — "in the gate" meaning in public, as it is said (Isaiah 3:15), "What do you mean that you crush My people, and grind the faces of the poor?" "For the Lord will plead their cause" — since they have no one to support them and to argue and plead their cause; "and spoil the soul of those who spoil them" — after the cry of the poor has been brought before Him, He will not take money from you in place of the robbery you committed, but will take your very soul as forfeit. And it is said (Job 27:8), "For what is the hope of the impious, though he has gained, when God takes away his soul?" And it is said (Proverbs 1:19), "So are the ways of every one that is greedy for gain; it takes away the life of its possessors." And whoever causes a widow or an orphan to cry out and be distressed, whether through robbery, oppression, humiliation, or any kind of pain, is liable to death at the hand of Heaven. And likewise judges who have it in their power to rescue the robbed from the hand of the oppressor and the orphan, and do not judge — the sentence of death is upon them, as it is said (Exodus 22:21-23), "You shall not afflict any widow or orphan child. If you afflict them at all, and they cry at all unto Me, I will surely hear their cry, and My wrath shall grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children fatherless." Its meaning: "and your wives shall be widows," corresponding to the affliction of the widow, "and your children fatherless," corresponding to the affliction of the orphan — measure for measure. And whoever distresses any man of Israel, even though these particular punishments are not written concerning him, transgresses a negative commandment, as it is said (Leviticus 25:17), "You shall not wrong one another"; and our Sages of blessed memory said, Scripture speaks here of wronging through words — and this too is a matter of distress and anguish, in the sense of (Isaiah 49:26), "and I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh." And our Sages of blessed memory said: all the gates [of prayer] are locked except the gates of wronging [through words]. And in the place where Scripture speaks of wronging through money, it mentions there buying and selling, as it is said (Leviticus 25:14), "And if you sell anything to your neighbor..." And they said: wronging through words is greater than wronging through money, for the one affects the body and the other affects the money; and concerning the one it is said (Leviticus 25:17), "and you shall fear your God," while concerning the other, "and you shall fear" is not said.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:25: And usury and interest carry a negative commandment, as it is said (Leviticus 25:36), "Take no interest or increase from him," and it is converted into a positive commandment, as it is said (ibid.), "that your brother may live with you" — its meaning: if you have taken interest or increase from him, you must surely restore it to your brother, so that he may live with you. And its punishment is exceedingly grave: as long as he has not corrected the wrong, he does not come to the resurrection of the dead, as it is said (Ezekiel 18:13), "He has given forth upon interest, and has taken increase: shall he then live? He shall not live" — and our Sages of blessed memory explained this concerning the matter of the resurrection of the dead. And our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever has the iniquity of interest in his hand, no angel pleads merit for him. And this is the meaning of "shall he then live?" — spoken in the form of a question and of astonishment: Is there an advocate to say that his sentence is to live? All shall answer and say, He shall not live.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:26: The Fourth Level – a Prohibition That Involves No Action: our Sages of blessed memory said, for a prohibition that involves no action, one is not lashed. And it is explained in their words, of blessed memory, that a prohibition involving no action is graver than a prohibition convertible into a positive commandment. And among the warnings that involve no action are warnings that depend on the heart, some on the tongue, and some on the withholding of one's hand and refraining from an action. And likewise there are transgressions that involve no action and depend on the sense of hearing and the sense of sight. And we have seen many people who have forgotten many of these; and there are some who know them yet are not careful about them, because they do not depend on an action — for the transgressions that depend on an action, such as eating forbidden fat, blood, carrion, or torn animals, one is not likely to stumble into them as readily as into transgressions committed through thought, through speech, or through refraining from an action. Therefore we saw fit to mention some of them, to remind and warn one who does not know how to be careful; and we have not come to elaborate on them, but only to allude to them, as a reminder for those who return from transgression.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:27: Among the warnings that depend on the heart: "Take heed lest you forget the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 8:11). And our Sages of blessed memory said: everywhere it says "take heed," "lest," or "do not," this is a negative commandment. We have been warned by this to remember the Blessed Name at all times. And a person is obligated to strive always to acquire for his own soul the modes of conduct required by such remembrance, such as fear, modesty, the ordering of one's thoughts, and the arrangement of one's character traits; for the holy seed will attain every proper and crowning conduct through the remembrance of the exalted Name, as it is said (Isaiah 45:25), "In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified and shall glory."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:28: "Take heed to yourself, and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes have seen" (Deuteronomy 4:9). And our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever forgets a single item of his learning transgresses two negative commandments. Might one think this applies even if his study overpowered him [and he could not help forgetting]? Scripture teaches, "and lest they depart from your heart" — Scripture speaks only of one who removes them from his heart by being idle from Torah and not meditating on it continually.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:29: "Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God has thrust them out from before you, saying, For my righteousness the Lord has brought me in to possess this land... Not for your righteousness, or for the uprightness of your heart, etc." (Deuteronomy 9:4). We have been warned by this not to imagine to ourselves that our success comes from our own righteousness and the uprightness of our heart, but rather to believe and know in our heart that our success comes from the kindness of the Most High and the abundance of His goodness — in the manner of what Jacob our father, peace upon him, said (Genesis 32:11), "I am too small for all the mercies and all the truth [You have shown Your servant]."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:30: "You shall not test the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 6:16). We have been warned by this that a man should not say, Let me test whether, through the service of charity, the Lord will prosper my way, and I will examine, through the success of my deeds, whether silver and gold will multiply for me. And a good man's hands are not found weakened even if his toil, though pursued with wisdom, knowledge, and skill of action, does not succeed in the matter of acquiring money and other bodily goods. And our Sages of blessed memory said that only regarding the commandment of tithes was such a test permitted, as it is said (Malachi 3:10), "Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be food in My house, and test Me now in this." Solomon the king, peace upon him, says (Proverbs 3:9-11), "Honor the Lord with your substance, and with the first-fruits of all your increase; so shall your barns be filled with plenty... My son, do not despise the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary of His correction." Its meaning: if it should not turn out for you that your barns be filled with plenty, when you have given of your substance and the first-fruits of all your increase to the service of charity, but rather the days of poverty seize hold of you — do not despise the discipline of the Lord, and know that this too is for your good; for "whom the Lord loves He rebukes," in order to do him good in his latter end, so that this be in exchange for the reward of this world and in place of its honor — a true reward and a hidden good that stands forever, for all eternity.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:31: "If you shall say in your heart, These nations are more numerous than I; how can I dispossess them? You shall not be afraid of them" (Deuteronomy 7:17-18).
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:32: "When you go out to battle, etc., and see horses and chariots, and a people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid of them" (Deuteronomy 20:1). We have been warned by this that if a man sees that trouble is near, the salvation of the Lord should be in his heart, and he should trust in it, as it is said (Psalms 85:10), "Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him," and so it is written (Isaiah 51:12), "Who are you, that you should be afraid of a man that shall die?"
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:33: "You shall not be afraid of the face of any man, for the judgment is God's" (Deuteronomy 1:17). We have been warned by this to believe that no harm will befall us on account of righteous judgment, when we show no favoritism in it, as our Sages of blessed memory said: messengers sent to perform a mitzvah suffer no harm, neither in their going nor in their return. And this is the explanation of "for the judgment is God's" — that no harm shall come to you on its account.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:34: "That his heart not be lifted up above his brethren" (Deuteronomy 17:20). We have been warned by this to remove from our soul the trait of pride, and that the great should not exalt himself over the small; and even the king himself should not lift up his heart above his brethren, and even if he must rule over them and does indeed exercise authority in his governance, he must nevertheless be lowly of spirit. And pride is among the grave transgressions that destroy and consume the soul, as it is said (Proverbs 16:5), "An abomination to the Lord is every proud heart." And what benefit is the acquiring of his silver and the abundance of his wealth and his treasures on high, seeing that afterward the heights of his glorious greatness become abominable and putrid, sunk deeper than Sheol? And let no wise man glory in anything but the service of the Blessed Name, His fear, trust in Him, love of Him, and cleaving to Him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:21), "He is your praise and He is your God," and it is said (Jeremiah 9:23), "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, etc., but let him who glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me."
